@graph.name: Five outgoing centers in a 16-realization cube move
Five outgoing centers in a 16-realization cube move
@graph.headline: Five outgoing centers in a 16-realization cube move
@graph.description: One fixed algebraic crossed boundary admits an incoming exponent-16 realization and at least five distinct outgoing centers, exceeding the stated maximum-three expectation.
@graph.abstract: We specify six algebraic boundary points, an incoming center, and at least five distinct outgoing centers for a cube move of 16-realizations. Existence follows from strict rational sign bounds for two continuous one-variable residuals. The boundary parameters are uniquely defined real roots of monotone polynomials. This contradicts the at-most-three expectation for construction curves sharing a focus in Remark 4.8 of Melotti–Ramassamy–Thévenin, in the realization setting allowing crossings. The fixed boundary is crossed, so the example concerns no proper embedding. Neither the exact number of centers for this boundary nor a universal maximum is determined.

@graph.name: Negative answers to the printed totally mixed face questions
Negative answers to the printed totally mixed face questions
@graph.headline: Negative answers to the printed totally mixed face questions
@graph.description: Two lattice 5-polytopes refute Payne’s printed totally mixed face claims: a disconnected, nonshellable order complex with rational Betti numbers (2,22).
@graph.abstract: For two polytopes, retain the faces of their Minkowski sum whose two canonical summands have positive dimensions and whose dimension is the sum of those dimensions. This is the definition in Payne’s printed Oberwolfach question. Let D be the standard four-simplex and I = [0,1]. For the full-dimensional lattice polytopes D × I and (−D) × I in ℝ⁵, the qualifying-face order complex is a disjoint union of two connected pure graphs, each with 50 vertices and 60 edges. Its rational Betti numbers are (2,22,0,…). Thus both printed assertions, shellability and the homology of a wedge of three-spheres, fail. The shared interval factor deliberately produces a nongeneric example. The argument concerns the printed additive-dimension definition; it does not settle shellability for the different mixed faces used in stable tropical intersections.

whole_expected_ScholarlyArticle.name: A singleton-supported cycle correction to Byrnes's differential-poset bound
whole_expected_ScholarlyArticle.headline: A singleton-supported cycle correction to Byrnes's differential-poset bound
whole_expected_ScholarlyArticle.description: An explicit singleton-supported cycle correction improves Byrnes’s cumulative differential-poset bound, with a sharp coefficient and conditional equality results.
whole_expected_ScholarlyArticle.abstract: For every ordinary unweighted r-differential poset and n ≥ 2, we subtract an explicit nonnegative term from Byrnes's cumulative upper bound for the nth rank size. The term is the cycle rank of the preceding incidence subgraph supported on elements with a singleton successor. Singleton witnesses transfer these cycles into the next incidence graph by replacing stars with trees having the same terminals. The correction can be positive and attained on standard reflected Young-prefix examples, and its coefficient one is sharp. A singleton-successor condition gives the conjectured local recurrence; two such successors give a conditional equality characterization. The result answers the printed request for an improvement of Byrnes's inequality in an incidence-dependent form. It does not prove the general local recurrence, improve the global Fibonacci envelope, or give a combinatorial proof of strict rank growth.

whole_expected_ScholarlyArticle.name: An exact period criterion for focal-distance products in elliptic billiards
whole_expected_ScholarlyArticle.headline: An exact period criterion for focal-distance products in elliptic billiards
whole_expected_ScholarlyArticle.description: An exact least-period criterion classifies when ordinary focal-distance products are constant in noncircular elliptic billiards, including primitive windings and repetitions.
whole_expected_ScholarlyArticle.abstract: For a noncircular elliptic billiard with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, we prove that the product of ordinary distances from all vertices to either fixed focus is independent of phase if and only if the least period is 2 modulo 4. This proves the least-period interpretation of entry k₁₁₄ in Reznik–Garcia–Koiller's list of unproved invariants and classifies every other primitive period and every repeated traversal. The proof identifies the complete divisor of the focal-distance factor in the classical Jacobi parameter. An exact doubled-triangle example shows why a condition on return length alone is insufficient. The parametrization, identities and divisor method are established tools. This AI-assisted research note is unrefereed.
